#### Loading data
```{r}
data <- read.csv("TCGA-PANCAN-HiSeq-801x20531/data.csv")
labels <- read.csv("TCGA-PANCAN-HiSeq-801x20531/labels.csv")

dim(data)
dim(labels)

data[1:5, 1:6]
head(labels)

# Checks: sample IDs line up, and no missing values
all(data[, 1] == labels[, 1])
sum(is.na(data))
sum(is.na(labels))
```

#### Exploration
```{r}
# 1. Target Class Frequency Distribution
class_table <- table(labels$Class)
class_df <- as.data.frame(class_table)
colnames(class_df) <- c("CancerType", "Count")

cat("Target Class Counts:\n")
class_df

ggplot(class_df, aes(x = reorder(CancerType, -Count), y = Count, fill = CancerType)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), vjust = -0.3, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Figure 1: Sample Distribution Across 5 Primary Cancer Types",
       x = "Cancer Type", y = "Number of Samples")

# 2. Log2 Transformation: log2(x + 1)
Class <- factor(labels$Class)
gene_matrix <- data[, sapply(data, is.numeric)]   # drops the sample-ID column
expr_log <- log2(gene_matrix + 1)

summary(expr_log[, 1])

# 3. Variance filtering and PCA (all samples, for the exploratory plot only)
gene_vars_all <- apply(expr_log, 2, var)
top_1000_all <- head(order(gene_vars_all, decreasing = TRUE), 1000)
pca_all <- prcomp(expr_log[, top_1000_all], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

pca_df <- data.frame(
  PC1 = pca_all$x[, 1],
  PC2 = pca_all$x[, 2],
  CancerType = Class
)
var_explained <- round(summary(pca_all)$importance[2, 1:2] * 100, 1)

ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = CancerType)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Figure 2: 2D PCA Projection of Top Variable Genes",
       x = paste0("PC1 (", var_explained[1], "% Variance)"),
       y = paste0("PC2 (", var_explained[2], "% Variance)"),
       color = "Cancer Type")
```

#### Train/test split and preprocessing for modeling (training data only)
```{r}
library(MASS)       
library(class)
library(e1071)
library(nnet)
library(randomForest)

set.seed(1)
train <- sample(1:nrow(expr_log), 560)            # about 70%
test  <- (1:nrow(expr_log))[-train]
Class.train <- Class[train]
Class.test  <- Class[test]

# Variance filter and PCA using ONLY the training rows
gene_vars <- apply(expr_log[train, ], 2, var)
top_genes <- order(gene_vars, decreasing = TRUE)[1:1000]
pr.out <- prcomp(expr_log[train, top_genes], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# PC scores: training from the PCA, test projected with the same PCA
train.pc30 <- pr.out$x[, 1:30]
test.pc30  <- predict(pr.out, expr_log[test, top_genes])[, 1:30]

dim(train.pc30); dim(test.pc30)
table(Class.train); table(Class.test)
```

### Method 1 (LDA)

#### LDA with PC = 10
```{r}
npc <- 10

train.df <- data.frame(Class = Class.train, train.pc30[, 1:npc])
test.df  <- data.frame(test.pc30[, 1:npc])

# LDA fitted model
lda.fit   <- lda(Class ~ ., data = train.df)
lda.pred  <- predict(lda.fit, test.df)
lda.class <- lda.pred$class

# Summary
table(lda.class, Class.test)
mean(lda.class == Class.test)
```

#### Finding optimal PC for LDA using CV
```{r}
set.seed(1)
folds <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = length(Class.train)))

npcs   <- c(2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30)
cv.err <- matrix(NA, 10, length(npcs), dimnames = list(NULL, npcs))

for (j in 1:10) {                      # j = which fold is held out
  for (i in seq_along(npcs)) {         # i = which number of PCs we're trying
    x <- train.pc30[, 1:npcs[i], drop = FALSE]
    fit  <- lda(x[folds != j, , drop = FALSE], Class.train[folds != j])
    pred <- predict(fit, x[folds == j, , drop = FALSE])$class
    cv.err[j, i] <- mean(pred != Class.train[folds == j])
  }
}

colMeans(cv.err)
```

PC = 5 wins because it has the lowest error and it is also the lowest number.

#### Using LDA with PC = 5
```{r}
npc <- 5

train.df <- data.frame(Class = Class.train, train.pc30[, 1:npc])
test.df  <- data.frame(test.pc30[, 1:npc])

# LDA fitted model
lda.fit   <- lda(Class ~ ., data = train.df)
lda.pred  <- predict(lda.fit, test.df)
lda.class <- lda.pred$class

# Summary
table(lda.class, Class.test)
lda.acc <- mean(lda.class == Class.test)
lda.acc
```

LDA accuracy = 1.

### Method 2 (QDA)

#### Finding PC for QDA using CV
```{r}
npcs <- c(2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30)
cv.err.qda <- matrix(NA, 10, length(npcs), dimnames = list(NULL, npcs))

for (j in 1:10) {
  for (i in seq_along(npcs)) {
    x <- train.pc30[, 1:npcs[i], drop = FALSE]
    fit  <- qda(x[folds != j, , drop = FALSE], Class.train[folds != j])
    pred <- predict(fit, x[folds == j, , drop = FALSE])$class
    cv.err.qda[j, i] <- mean(pred != Class.train[folds == j])
  }
}

colMeans(cv.err.qda)
```

The best PC for QDA is 5 because it has a 0.000000000 or 0% of error.

#### Using QDA with PC = 5
```{r}
npc <- 5

train.df <- data.frame(Class = Class.train, train.pc30[, 1:npc])
test.df  <- data.frame(test.pc30[, 1:npc])

# QDA fitted model
qda.fit   <- qda(Class ~ ., data = train.df)
qda.pred  <- predict(qda.fit, test.df)
qda.class <- qda.pred$class

# Summary
table(qda.class, Class.test)
qda.acc <- mean(qda.class == Class.test)
qda.acc
```

QDA accuracy = 1

### Method 3 (: Multinomial logistic regression)

#### Finding PC for multinomial using CV
```{r}
cv.err.mn <- matrix(NA, 10, length(npcs), dimnames = list(NULL, npcs))

for (j in 1:10) {
  for (i in seq_along(npcs)) {
    d <- data.frame(Class = Class.train, train.pc30[, 1:npcs[i], drop = FALSE])
    fit  <- multinom(Class ~ ., data = d[folds != j, ], maxit = 500, trace = FALSE)
    pred <- predict(fit, newdata = d[folds == j, ])
    cv.err.mn[j, i] <- mean(pred != Class.train[folds == j])
  }
}

colMeans(cv.err.mn)
```

The best PC for Multinomial logistic regression is 5 because it has 0.001785714 or 0.179% error.

#### Using multinomial with PC = 5
```{r}
npc <- 5

train.df <- data.frame(Class = Class.train, train.pc30[, 1:npc])
test.df  <- data.frame(test.pc30[, 1:npc])

# Multinomial fitted model
mn.fit   <- multinom(Class ~ ., data = train.df, maxit = 500, trace = FALSE)
mn.class <- predict(mn.fit, test.df)

# Summary
table(mn.class, Class.test)
mn.acc <- mean(mn.class == Class.test)
mn.acc
```

### Method 4 (KNN)

#### Finding PC and k for KNN
```{r}
ks <- c(1, 3, 5, 10, 15)
knn.err <- matrix(NA, length(npcs), length(ks), dimnames = list(npcs, ks))

set.seed(1)
for (i in seq_along(npcs)) {            # i = number of PCs
  for (m in seq_along(ks)) {            # m = value of k
    e <- numeric(10)
    for (j in 1:10) {                   # j = held-out fold
      x <- train.pc30[, 1:npcs[i], drop = FALSE]
      pred <- knn(x[folds != j, , drop = FALSE],
                  x[folds == j, , drop = FALSE],
                  Class.train[folds != j], k = ks[m])
      e[j] <- mean(pred != Class.train[folds == j])
    }
    knn.err[i, m] <- mean(e)
  }
}

round(knn.err, 4)
```

We pick PC = 10 and k = 5 because it has the lowest error with 0.0018 or 0.18%

#### Using KNN with PC = 10, k = 5
```{r}
npc <- 10

set.seed(1)
knn.class <- knn(train.pc30[, 1:npc], test.pc30[, 1:npc], Class.train, k = 5)

# Summary
table(knn.class, Class.test)
knn.acc <- mean(knn.class == Class.test)
knn.acc
```

KNN accuracy = 1

### Method 5 (Random forest)

#### Finding mtry for random forest using OOB error
```{r}
train.genes <- data.frame(Class = Class.train, expr_log[train, top_genes])

mtrys   <- c(10, 32, 100)
oob.err <- rep(NA, length(mtrys))

set.seed(1)
for (m in seq_along(mtrys)) {
  rf <- randomForest(Class ~ ., data = train.genes, mtry = mtrys[m], ntree = 500)
  oob.err[m] <- rf$err.rate[500, "OOB"]
}

data.frame(mtry = mtrys, OOB.error = round(oob.err, 4))
```

We choose mtry = 100 because it has the lowest error

#### Using random forest with mtry = 100
```{r}
set.seed(1)
rf.fit <- randomForest(Class ~ ., data = train.genes, mtry = 100,
                       ntree = 500, importance = TRUE)
rf.class <- predict(rf.fit, newdata = expr_log[test, top_genes])

# Summary
table(rf.class, Class.test)
rf.acc <- mean(rf.class == Class.test)
rf.acc
```

Random Forest accuracy = 1

### Comparing the methods

```{r}
results <- data.frame(
  Method  = c("LDA", "QDA", "Multinomial", "KNN", "Random forest"),
  Setting = c("5 PCs", "5 PCs", "5 PCs", "10 PCs, k = 5", "mtry = 100"),
  CV.Error = round(unname(c(colMeans(cv.err)["5"],
                            colMeans(cv.err.qda)["5"],
                            colMeans(cv.err.mn)["5"],
                            knn.err["10", "5"],
                            oob.err[3])), 4),
  Test.Accuracy = c(lda.acc, qda.acc, mn.acc, knn.acc, rf.acc)
)
results$Test.Mistakes <- round((1 - results$Test.Accuracy) * length(Class.test))

results
```

### Interpreting the results

#### What the PCs capture
```{r}
pve <- 100 * pr.out$sdev^2 / sum(pr.out$sdev^2)
round(cumsum(pve)[c(2, 5, 10, 20, 30)], 1)    # cumulative % of variance

# genes with the largest weights (loadings) on PC1 and PC2
head(sort(abs(pr.out$rotation[, 1]), decreasing = TRUE), 10)
head(sort(abs(pr.out$rotation[, 2]), decreasing = TRUE), 10)
```

#### Important genes from the random forest
```{r}
importance(rf.fit)[order(-importance(rf.fit)[, "MeanDecreaseGini"])[1:10], ]

varImpPlot(rf.fit, n.var = 15, type = 2)
```

                   Gene  = rep(top3, each = nrow(train.genes)),
